title: Nested Integral Generator Theorem: From Operator Tautologies to Families of Exact Integral Identities
abstract: Inserting resolutions of the identity is a standard technique for representing states and operators throughout quantum theory, quantum field theory, and related areas of mathematical physics. This paper elevates this procedure to a rigorous, representation-independent framework through the Nested Integral Generator Theorem. Starting from operator tautologies, the theorem systematically generates exact multi-fold integral identities by successive insertions of continuous resolutions of the identity followed by projection onto arbitrary orthonormal basis vectors. The resulting construction applies to arbitrary finite compositions of closed operators acting on arbitrary target states and establishes a general mapping from operator equalities to families of exact integral identities. Using the theory of vector-valued integration, explicit and verifiable sufficient conditions are derived under which inner products may be interchanged rigorously with Bochner integrals, thereby placing a step that is often left implicit in the physics literature on a firm mathematical foundation. As an immediate consequence, the theorem yields exact integral representations for individual operator functions. Its scope is illustrated through elementary, polynomial, and analytic single-mode operators, as well as single- and two-mode Gaussian unitaries, including squeezing and beam splitting. The framework is further applied to two nontrivial examples beyond standard Gaussian calculations: an exact integral representation of a Kerr-squeezed coherent-state overlap and exact Fock-basis matrix elements for a composite two-mode Gaussian network expressed in terms of bivariate Hermite polynomials.
summary: This paper introduces the Nested Integral Generator Theorem, a rigorous mathematical framework to convert operator equalities into multi-fold exact integral identities. By systematically using resolutions of the identity, it provides universal tools to calculate matrix elements for complex systems in continuous-variable quantum optics, such as those involving squeezing and nonlinear Kerr interactions.
main_problem: To establish a rigorous, representation-independent mathematical framework for calculating complex operator compositions by systematically converting them into exact multi-fold integral identities.
main_result: The Nested Integral Generator Theorem provides an exact $N$-fold nested integral representation for matrix elements involving chains of operators, applicable to various quantum systems.
method: The core method involves starting from operator tautologies and iteratively inserting continuous resolutions of the identity, utilizing vector-valued integration theory to rigorously justify the interchange of inner products with Bochner integrals.
model_or_system: The framework is applied to continuous-variable bosonic systems, including single-mode operators, two-mode Gaussian unitaries (squeezing, beam splitting), and nonlinear interactions like the Kerr effect. It provides exact calculations for matrix elements $\langle n| \mathcal{O} | \alpha, \lambda angle$.
key_observables: Exact integral representations of operator functions, such as the overlap between a Kerr-squeezed coherent state and Fock states, and two-mode Gaussian network matrix elements.
important_parameters: Squeezing parameters ($\zeta$), beam-splitter angles ($\varphi$), Kerr nonlinearity strength ($\chi$), and photon number ($n, m$).
main_assumptions: The primary assumptions involve the existence of a continuous resolution of the identity and meeting verifiable sufficient conditions (Bochner integrability) to interchange integration and projection operators.

why_interesting: It provides a powerful, systematic tool that replaces potentially intractable direct calculation or approximation methods (like Trotter expansions) with exact integral formulas for complex quantum optical processes.
